name: Annotate
description: Mark up your own screenshot on your device - arrows, boxes, numbered steps, callouts, highlighter and a spotlight dim.

examples.label: Point at it and say why

inputs.label: Picture
inputs.help: A JPEG, PNG, WebP, GIF or SVG. It is read in your browser and never leaves your device; you can also drop it straight onto the canvas. PDF pages are out of scope here - export the page as an image first, or use Redact for a PDF. Without a picture the tool draws a placeholder screen so the marks still have something to sit on.

inputs.label: Marks
inputs.help: Every mark is a row. Draw on the picture to add one, drag a mark to move it, drag its corner dot to resize, tap the cross to take it off. Numbers on step pins are counted for you.

fields.label: X
fields.help: Left edge as a percentage of the picture's width. An arrow starts here.

fields.label: Y
fields.help: Top edge as a percentage of the picture's height. An arrow starts here.

fields.label: Width
fields.help: Percentage of the picture's width. An arrow reads it as the horizontal run to its point, so it may be negative.

fields.label: Height
fields.help: Percentage of the picture's height. An arrow reads it as the vertical run to its point, so it may be negative.

fields.label: Label
fields.help: Words for a callout, or an optional caption beside a step pin. A step pin's number is worked out from its position in this list, so there is nothing to type.

inputs.label: Accent
inputs.help: One colour for every mark. Callouts and pins put their words in whichever of black or white reads better on it.

inputs.label: Line weight
inputs.help: Scales with the picture, so the same weight looks the same on a phone grab and a 4K screenshot.

inputs.label: Mark style
inputs.help: Sketchy gives every line a slight hand-drawn wobble. The wobble is worked out from the mark's position in the list, so it never changes between renders or between the preview and the file you download.

inputs.label: Text read request
inputs.help: Written by the Snap to text button on the canvas, never shown. A new value asks the tool to read the picture with the on-device text reader and offer each text line as an anchor to place a mark on; "off" cancels a read in progress. Anchors are only ever offered - a mark is added when you click one.
